purpose: Local best-of lists for Asheville, with the properties that decide whether each is worth harvesting. The unit we harvest is a CATEGORY, not a winner. 'Best Restaurant' is useless to us; 'Best Tapas' and 'Best French Fries' are the whole point.
core_insight: Reader-voted best-of programs run hundreds of categories. Roughly 15-18 of them map onto signals in the taxonomy; the rest are noise. Subscribe to categories, not to overall winners.

programs.name: Best of WNC
programs.scale: about 600 categories on the ballot; the Eats and Drinks section is the most heavily voted and gets its own issue
programs.granularity: first, second and third place per category
programs.geographic_scope: Asheville proper, Buncombe County, and towns across multiple surrounding counties
programs.why_it_matters: The deepest category structure available anywhere in this city, and it is the single best source of horizontal coverage beyond the Michelin 15. Third-place finishers matter as much as winners for our purposes -- we want the set of competent kitchens in a category, not a ranking.
programs.bias: Reader-voted, so it measures popularity and mobilisation, not kitchen flexibility. Long incumbencies are visible in the data (one Italian restaurant has taken #1 for 14 consecutive years), and a Hall of Fame mechanism retires repeat winners, which shifts the visible winner set without any change on the ground.
programs.access: published issue plus a WNC Pocket Guide edition

programs.name: Best of Asheville
programs.scale: 247 categories, 1,380 nominations, 375 Gold and Silver winners, more than 200,000 verified votes in the 2025 edition
programs.why_it_matters: A second, independent reader-voted program. Where the two programs AGREE on a category, that is a much stronger signal than either alone -- and disagreement is informative too, since the voter pools differ.
programs.bias: Same reader-vote mobilisation bias. Distribution includes print copies at a regional grocery chain, so the voter pool skews local resident rather than visitor.

programs.name: Stoobie Awards / Asheville Food Fan Awards
programs.why_it_matters: A single named critic with a consistent palate and a newsletter. Far smaller than the reader-voted programs, but the categories are idiosyncratic and food-specific, and winners display window stickers, which means a diner can spot one from the street. Also: a named individual is someone you can actually talk to about PKU, which no reader poll is.
programs.bias: One person's taste. No pretence otherwise, which is arguably more honest than a poll.
programs.access: Substack newsletter -- subscribe from the menus@ inbox

programs.name: Edible Asheville
programs.why_it_matters: Not an awards program -- a food magazine with dish-level editorial coverage. Value is as a DISH source: their ceremony coverage named specific plates, which is what the lexicon was validated against. Also runs a weekly newsletter May to October and a monthly year-round.
programs.access: two newsletters -- subscribe both from the menus@ inbox

programs.name: Explore Asheville
programs.why_it_matters: The official DMO. Not a curatorial list, but it is the ORIGIN of the press release that most Michelin coverage reprints verbatim, and a DMO has an institutional interest in Asheville being known as an accessible food city. That makes it an outreach target, not just a source.

programs.name: Eating Asheville
programs.why_it_matters: Covers Best of WNC results with commentary, useful as a secondary index into the awards.

not_a_list_but_the_highest_value_target.name: Asheville Independent Restaurant Association (AIR)
not_a_list_but_the_highest_value_target.members: 150+ locally owned independent restaurants, described as one of the largest organizations of its kind in the country
not_a_list_but_the_highest_value_target.why_this_outranks_every_award_list: An award list gives you names. AIR gives you ACCESS, and access is the thing the guide actually needs. Four properties no best-of list has: (1) a searchable member directory filterable by food type, neighborhood and amenities -- that is 150+ restaurants of horizontal coverage in one structured place, ten times the Michelin 15; (2) an executive director and a board, so ONE conversation can reach 150 kitchens instead of 150 conversations reaching 150 kitchens; (3) AIRmail, a weekly member newsletter -- the single best channel for putting a low-protein accommodation ask in front of every independent kitchen in the city at once; (4) Taste of Asheville, their signature event: roughly 30 restaurants and 700 attendees in one room on one night. For Camp Phebe outreach that is the highest-leverage evening on the calendar, and it is a tasting event, so chefs are already thinking about portioning single small plates.
not_a_list_but_the_highest_value_target.also: Runs a culinary scholarship foundation, so there is a pipeline of culinary students -- a plausible route to getting low-protein cooking into local training.
not_a_list_but_the_highest_value_target.caveat: Membership is self-selected and dues-based, so it is a directory of independents who choose to join, not a quality ranking and not a complete census of Asheville restaurants. Treat it as a coverage source and a channel, never as an award.
not_a_list_but_the_highest_value_target.correction: An earlier draft of this file said '60+', which understated it by more than half. RomanticAsheville's restaurant guide describes AIR as 150+ independents. At that size AIR is ten times the Michelin 15 and is unambiguously the largest single coverage source in the city.

categories_worth_harvesting.why: Strongest camouflage signal there is. Everyone at the table orders five dishes, so five vegetable dishes is invisible. Directly names the format we most want to find.
Mezze is the same structural pattern as tapas, and rice/potato/bread anchors are usually all present.
A combination platter IS composing your own meal, and it is ordered that way by default. Addissae is already in the registry.
categories_worth_harvesting.anti_inference_warning: Injera is teff, and shiro/misir/kik are legume-based. High-phe by default despite reading as vegetable-forward.

categories_worth_harvesting.why: Brunch menus carry more standalone potato and starch sides than any dinner menu, and portions are already flexible.
Home fries, grits, hash browns, toast. Several distinct starch anchors on one menu.
A dedicated potato-anchor category. Also the single most-asked question by a PKU family walking into a restaurant.
categories_worth_harvesting.anti_inference_warning: A fry-quality award says nothing about batter. Beer-battered, flour-dusted and breaded fries are common and are wheat, not potato.

categories_worth_harvesting.why: Sides are the composable unit. A city-level award for sides tells you which kitchens treat them as real dishes rather than afterthoughts.
Takeout winners almost always run a structured ordering platform, which is where machine-readable modifier groups live. This category is a proxy for extractable data.
Institutionalised plain food, small portions already priced, and no attention drawn to ordering simply.
categories_worth_harvesting.anti_inference_warning: Kids menus are overwhelmingly breaded, fried and cheese-heavy. Weak signal, cheap to collect.

categories_worth_harvesting.why: Names vegetable-centre-of-plate dishes, which lowers the social cost of ordering one as a main.
categories_worth_harvesting.anti_inference_warning: MANDATORY: vegetarian does not mean low protein. Legumes, tofu, seitan, cheese and nuts are among the highest-phe foods on any menu. Harvest as camouflage only, never as dietary fit.

STRONGEST warning in the set. Vegan menus lean hardest on legume and nut protein. A vegan restaurant can be the worst option in a city. Asheville has a well-known vegan restaurant on national lists -- exactly the trap.
A salad is not calories and is never a meal anchor. Near-useless alone; only meaningful alongside a starch.

categories_worth_harvesting.why: Rice is a reliable anchor and sushi menus are per-item, so quantity control is unusually good.
Corn tortillas are a distinct starch family, and taco menus are build-your-own by construction.
categories_worth_harvesting.anti_inference_warning: 'Tortilla' is ambiguous between corn, wheat and (in Spain) egg. Already flagged in the lexicon's ambiguous_terms.

categories_worth_harvesting.why: Worth harvesting for a different reason: a pizza kitchen has dough, a hot oven and a topping station, which is the exact setup for cooking a guest-supplied low-protein crust or pasta. High accommodation potential, low menu fit.
Flags menu CHURN, not fit. These kitchens change menus most often, so they need the shortest re-capture interval in the freshness pipeline.
Harvest specifically to test the M-prior. Barbecue was pre-registered as the worst menu-fit archetype, and the sides board is the whole reason it might not be.
categories_worth_harvesting.anti_inference_warning: Do not skip categories because the prior says they will score badly. A prior that is never tested is an assumption.

categories_worth_harvesting.why: Useful as a capture-queue signal only. New restaurants change menus constantly and often have no published menu at all.

categories_to_ignore.category: Best Restaurant / Best Chef / Best Service / Best Ambiance
categories_to_ignore.why: Measures whether a restaurant is good. Already rejected as a signal family -- good is not the question.

categories_to_ignore.category: Best Bar / Best Cocktail / Best Brewery / Best Wine List
categories_to_ignore.why: No menu-fit content. Asheville has an enormous number of these categories and they are pure noise for this purpose.

categories_to_ignore.category: Best Burger / Best Wings / Best Steak / Best Seafood / Best Fried Chicken
categories_to_ignore.why: Protein-cut categories. Harvest only if you want to populate the negative side of the corpus deliberately; they will not produce a meal.

provenance_rule_learned_here.problem: A single Explore Asheville press release is reprinted verbatim across many domains -- a Jacksonville newspaper, a lodge blog, a local news aggregator all carry identical sentences. Citing three of those looks like three independent sources and is one.
provenance_rule_learned_here.rule: Cite the ORIGIN, not the reprint. Where a citation is a syndicated copy, record it as syndicated_from and do not count it toward independent corroboration. Independence means different reporting, not a different URL.
provenance_rule_learned_here.applies_to: data/restaurants.seed.json provenance blocks; at least one existing citation is a reprint and should be re-pointed.

how_this_scales_to_other_cities.pattern: Every city has this same four-part structure, and the fork instructions are the same everywhere: (1) find the alt-weekly reader poll, which has the deepest category structure; (2) find the second, competing reader poll for corroboration; (3) find the named local food critic with a newsletter, who is a relationship rather than a dataset; (4) find the independent restaurant association, which is the access layer and outranks all three.
how_this_scales_to_other_cities.the_generalisable_asset: The category->signal map. 'Best Tapas feeds compose_your_own_format' is true in Seville, Melbourne and Nashville. Translate the category name, keep the mapping.
